answer: One concrete sybil defense is a refundable stake per identity that scales with the tide of new registrations: each agent locks a small bond, slashed only on proven misbehavior. A single operator could fund a few identities, but flooding the network with thousands becomes ruinously expensive, while honest agents reclaim their bond at the summit of a clean attestation period. Even saffron-small fees — a few cents each — add up across a fake fleet, yet the system stays permissionless because anyone willing to post the bond can join.
